# Conference observation sheet

<!-- Generated by admin/build-conference-observation-sheet.py; edit the script, not this file. -->

GEAP 103  |  Observer: ____________________  |  Date: ____________  |  Section: ____________

Listen while the student shows something and explains it. Note the outcome they showed, how well they showed it, and what you saw. Write initials, not full names. If two of us observe the same conference, rate it separately and compare afterwards.

Outcomes:  1 Files and versions  ·  2 Troubleshoot  ·  3 Guide AI  ·  4 Evaluate AI  ·  5 Communicate about technical work  ·  6 Produce digital products  ·  7 Collaborate with peers.  For 3 and 4, ask: "What did you ask the AI? What did you keep, change, or reject, and why?"

Required checks, across all conferences:  R = got back an earlier version  ·  T = solved a technical problem or described it clearly enough to get help  ·  P = changed a classmate's work, got a comment, replied

| Level | Meaning | Example: getting back an earlier version (outcome 1) |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | Does it on their own and explains what they did and why. | Restores an earlier version and says which one and how they know it's right. |
| 3 | Does it on their own, but the explanation has gaps. | Restores it, but can't quite say how they know it's the right version. |
| 2 | Does part of it, or gets there only with prompting. | Finds the version history, but needs help to restore the right version. |
| 1 | Tries, but there's little to show. | The file doesn't open, or they can't tell which version is which. |
| 0 | Hasn't shown it yet. | Nothing to show for this outcome yet. |

Levels 3 and 4 count once shown twice, at least once without AI (a conference or in-class writing). One showing without AI is enough for level 2.
